name: vLLM 0.20 TTFT for Qwen3.5-9B at 32K-256K context (dense FA2, chunk 4K)
methodology: Serving: vLLM 0.20, chunk 4K, dense baseline FA2. Context: 32K tokens. Hardware: GPU 80G (specific GPU model not stated). Concurrency: not explicitly stated (likely single-request or low concurrency given TTFT measurement). Cache state: cold (no prefix caching mentioned). Output: first token only. Value 2944 ms at 32K. Sibling points from same leaderboard: 64K = 6863 ms, 100K = 11780 ms, 128K = 17652 ms, 256K = 50915 ms.
notes:
Published by SOTA2 Research (formerly WizWand) on 2026-06-05. Part of a TTFT leaderboard spanning 32K-256K context. The 32K TTFT of 2.944s for a 9B model on an 80G GPU is notably high, suggesting either a very long prompt processing time or significant scheduling overhead. The scaling from 32K to 256K is roughly linear in context length (2.9s to 50.9s, ~17x for 8x context), which is consistent with O(L^2) attention dominating at long context. Sparse attention variant (distilled indexer) achieves 1.07x-1.93x speedup over dense.

So the aggregator page is now a Tier-C-author-preprint measurement.
